title: A basket on the river
hookLine: Musa's mother is inspired to set her baby on the Nile, and not to fear

cards: The first day of school. The car keys. The airport gate.
Parents hold on as long as they can, and then they open their hands. Now take that to Egypt, long ago.
Pharaoh has split the land into factions, and one people, the Children of Israel, he treats as the weak ones: their baby boys are being killed. A woman among them has just given birth to a son.
She's nursing him, hiding him, listening for footsteps. Then she is given an instruction that sounds like the opposite of everything a mother knows.

teach.b: Musa, peace be upon him, comes back again and again in the Qur'an, in pieces across many surahs. This piece is in Surah al-Qasas, the Stories. Allah inspired the mother of Musa: nurse him.
And when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear, and do not grieve. We will bring him back to you and make him one of the messengers. Look at the order.
First: nurse him. Hold him while you can.

teach.h: DO NOT FEAR, DO NOT GRIEVE.
teach.b: Then, when the fear comes, not before: the water. And two things forbidden to her: fear and grief. Not because there's nothing to fear, but because two promises have been made.
He'll come back to you. And he'll be a messenger.
The Qur'an calls this wahy, inspiration, the same word used for revelation to prophets, though scholars explain that for her it was inspiration placed in the heart, not prophecy.
A small surprise: the Qur'an's own word for what she used isn't basket. In Surah Ta-Ha it's tabut, a chest or box.

teach.h: WE WILL BRING HIM BACK TO YOU.
teach.b: The basket of reeds is how Exodus tells it. Either way, a mother closes a lid over her baby and sets him on the Nile. Most of what we'll hear about Musa is big: fire, staffs, a sea.
It begins here, with a woman opening her hands at the edge of a river, because she trusted what she had been told more than what she feared.

how: Muslims retell the story of Musa's mother as a model of trust in Allah (tawakkul), and her story in Surah al-Qasas is often recited and taught to children.

games.q: you're Musa's mother. Pharaoh's men are killing baby boys. you've been inspired: nurse him, and when you fear, cast him into the river. the fear comes. what do you do?
o: hide him deeper in the house.
set him on the river, as you were told.
flee Egypt with him in the night.
games.why: she set him on the Nile. with the instruction came two promises: he'll come back to you, and he'll be a messenger.

practice: Find the worry you've been nursing; her order was nurse him first, then the river, so first name the one thing you can still do about it today.

Then close the lid on the rest and set it on a slow, wide river, into Allah's hands, or, if that's not your language, just out of your own; you're not forgetting it, just trusting the river with the part you can't carry.
If you pray, name it as you let it go.

wordCard.voice: Tabut, the chest that carried baby Musa onto the Nile.

orig.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 20:39: a chest or box, the Qur'an's word for what carried baby Musa.

carryVoice: Your line: put it on the river. Two promises went down the river with him. Day forty-three.
